indicators.label: GDP growth
indicators.note: Annual % change in real GDP. The headline 'is the economy growing' number.

indicators.label: GDP per capita growth
indicators.note: Growth per person. Strips out the part of GDP growth that is just more people.

indicators.label: GDP per capita
indicators.note: Current US$. Cross-country comparison at market exchange rates.

indicators.label: GDP
indicators.note: Total economy size in current US$.

indicators.label: Inflation (CPI)
indicators.note: Annual consumer price inflation. Scored on distance from the central bank's target, so deflation counts against a country too.

indicators.label: Lending interest rate
indicators.note: What banks charge prime borrowers. A rough proxy for the cost of credit where a long policy-rate history is not available.

indicators.label: Real interest rate
indicators.note: Lending rate minus inflation. Neither high nor low is straightforwardly good.

indicators.label: Broad money growth
indicators.note: How fast the money supply is expanding.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.note: Modelled ILO estimate, so it is comparable across all five markets.

indicators.label: Youth unemployment
indicators.note: Ages 15-24. Usually the first rate to move when hiring freezes.

indicators.label: Labour force participation
indicators.note: Share of working-age people in the labour force.

indicators.label: Government debt
indicators.note: Central government debt as % of GDP. Patchy for Nigeria.

indicators.label: Fiscal balance
indicators.note: Net lending (+) or net borrowing (-) as % of GDP.

indicators.label: External debt stocks
indicators.note: Total external debt. Reported for developing economies, so Nigeria only.

indicators.label: Foreign direct investment
indicators.note: Net FDI inflows as % of GDP. Ireland's swings are enormous because of multinational balance-sheet moves, not factories being built.

indicators.label: FDI inflows (US$)
indicators.note: The same flow in dollars rather than as a share of GDP.

indicators.label: Portfolio equity inflows
indicators.note: Net foreign buying of listed shares. Hot money: it leaves fast.

indicators.label: Gross capital formation
indicators.note: Domestic investment as % of GDP. What the economy spends on its own future.

indicators.label: Stock market capitalisation
indicators.note: Listed domestic companies' market value as % of GDP. The long-run read on whether the stock market is growing relative to the economy.

indicators.label: Listed domestic companies
indicators.note: Company count on the domestic exchange. The closest long-run proxy for IPOs net of delistings: a falling count means take-privates are outpacing floats.

indicators.label: Stocks traded
indicators.note: Total value traded as % of GDP. High can mean liquidity or panic.

indicators.label: New business density
indicators.note: New limited-liability companies per 1,000 working-age adults. The best cross-country business-formation series, but it only starts in 2006.

indicators.label: New businesses registered
indicators.note: Absolute count of new company registrations.

indicators.label: Current account balance
indicators.note: Surplus (+) or deficit (-) as % of GDP. Whether the country is paying its own way.

indicators.label: Exports
indicators.note: Exports of goods and services as % of GDP.

indicators.label: Trade openness
indicators.note: Exports plus imports as % of GDP.

indicators.label: Reserves
indicators.note: Import cover in months. Below three months is the classic warning line.

indicators.label: Exchange rate vs US$
indicators.note: Local currency units per US dollar, annual average. Rising means depreciation.

indicators.label: Political stability
indicators.note: WGI estimate, roughly -2.5 to +2.5. Absence of violence and disorderly power transfer.

indicators.label: Government effectiveness
indicators.note: Quality of public services and policy implementation.

indicators.label: Regulatory quality
indicators.note: Whether policy lets the private sector function.

indicators.label: Rule of law
indicators.note: Contract enforcement, property rights, courts.

indicators.label: Control of corruption
indicators.note: How far public power is exercised for private gain.

indicators.label: Voice and accountability
indicators.note: Free expression, free media, ability to select a government.

indicators.label: Population
indicators.note: Used to put the absolute numbers in proportion.

markets_business.note: The stagflation comparison being drawn is to the late 1970s: 2% growth alongside 4.5% inflation.

A real policy rate that is still deeply restrictive at 26.5% against 15% inflation

markets_business.ipo: NGX listing activity is thin and not covered by the global IPO trackers. The World Bank listed-company count in the historical charts is the usable long-run series.
markets_business.note: Nigeria is the one market here where the free equity-index providers carry no usable NGX All-Share series, so the live market panel shows it as unavailable rather than guessing.

global.ipo: Global IPO proceeds tripled year on year in H1 2026, from $58.2bn to $178bn across 524 deals (up from 490). The concentration is extreme: the top 10 were almost all US, almost all AI-adjacent.
themes: Tariffs are the shared shock. They read as inflation in the US, as a growth and labour hit in Canada, and as a tax-base risk in Ireland.
Four of the five central banks are on hold. Nigeria is the outlier on level (26.5%) and the only one with disinflation as its main story rather than sticky inflation.
Energy prices from the Middle East conflict have pushed up the 2026 inflation forecast in Europe.
